title: EXCLUSIVE: Anthropic warns government attitudes may hurt customer ties, IPO prospectus shows
source_used: The Next Web (relaying Reuters); Yahoo Finance also read
key_facts: Reuters reported on Friday 2 Oct 2026, after seeing Anthropic's unpublished IPO prospectus, that Anthropic warns the US government's view of it could hurt ties with business customers and partners as well as its government work.
Per Reuters, government deals are less than 1% of Anthropic's annual revenue.

The filing points to clashes with Washington: the president told federal agencies in February to stop using Anthropic's models, and the Pentagon named the company a supply-chain risk; a judge temporarily blocked that label in March.

It also cites US Commerce Department export controls on two top Anthropic models in June; Anthropic disabled both for all customers on 12 June and restored access on 1 July after the controls were lifted.
Anthropic warned such steps could happen again and could damage its name with customers, partners, staff and investors whatever the final result.
Reuters said the listing could value Anthropic at up to $2 trillion; Yahoo Finance says the IPO could come as soon as mid-November.
The Next Web notes it has not seen the prospectus; it is relaying Reuters.
quote_evidence: Anthropic has warned that the US government's view of the company could hurt its ties with business customers and partners as well as its government work.
According to Reuters, the filing says government deals account for less than 1% of Anthropic's annual revenue.
To comply, Anthropic disabled both models for all customers on 12 June, then restored access on 1 July after the department lifted the controls.
why_it_matters_hint: Anthropic itself tells would-be investors that politics could cost it customers beyond government work, even though government deals are under 1% of revenue.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (Reuters exclusive on the prospectus); the prospectus was first reported by Reuters on 29 Sep 2026.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401). Text read from The Next Web's account of the Reuters report and a short Yahoo Finance item; the Business Standard page was cut off. The prospectus is not public and none of these outlets say they have seen it themselves, so everything is Reuters' account. Follow-up of the 29 Sep 2026 Reuters story on the same prospectus.
